messages.author: Veikko Vikkelä
messages.text: Hi Erkki, on TRN-118 I replaced the optical module. Link is UP and receive power is in range, but traffic counters haven't moved for five minutes. Anything familiar?

messages.author: Erkki Expert
messages.text: I've seen that on this older platform after an optic swap. First compare counters at both ends and check that the peer isn't administratively blocked.

messages.author: Veikko Vikkelä
messages.text: Peer is clear. Both ends show link up, but counters are still flat.

messages.author: Erkki Expert
messages.text: That points more toward stale forwarding state than a bad optic. In the approved maintenance window, try a scoped disable/enable of the interface; avoid rebooting the node unless that doesn't recover it.

messages.author: Veikko Vikkelä
messages.text: Done within the window. Counters are moving and service is back 👍

messages.author: Erkki Expert
messages.text: Good. That has been my experience with this model, but note the platform and symptoms so nobody treats it as a universal SFP fix.

messages.author: Aino Aalto
messages.text: MW-204 dropped modulation twice during the rain. BER spiked but recovered both times. Should we send someone to realign the dish?

messages.author: Mika Ranta
messages.text: Before dispatch, compare the far-end level and weather timestamps. In my experience, a brief dip that tracks heavy rain at both ends is different from a persistent alignment shift.

messages.author: Aino Aalto
messages.text: Both ends dipped together and returned to their previous level between showers. No recent site work.

messages.author: Mika Ranta
messages.text: I'd monitor through the weather and compare the dry-weather baseline. If the level stays shifted or one end behaves differently, then investigate alignment or hardware.

messages.author: Aino Aalto
messages.text: Rain has eased; level is back at baseline and no new BER spike. Keeping the watch open for now.

messages.author: Noora Heikkinen
messages.text: After the access migration, only VLAN 317 has intermittent loss. Ports are up and physical counters look clean.

messages.author: Jari Salmi
messages.text: I've run into this when a temporary handoff disagrees about tagging. Compare the VLAN mode and allowed list at both ends before changing the trunk.

messages.author: Noora Heikkinen
messages.text: Found it: upstream expects tagged, but the temporary patch port is treating 317 as native.

messages.author: Jari Salmi
messages.text: That matches the scope of the loss. Restore the approved service definition at both ends, then verify MAC learning and traffic. Don't broaden the allowed VLAN list as a workaround.

messages.author: Noora Heikkinen
messages.text: Corrected under the change. MAC learning is normal and loss is clear. I've noted that the temporary port was the exception.

messages.author: Kaisa Puro
messages.text: SYN-601 lost GNSS shortly after antenna maintenance. It's in holdover and the timing offset is climbing.

messages.author: Rami Lehto
messages.text: I saw a similar pattern after connector work. Check receiver alarms and the antenna path first, then confirm the alternate source is healthy before considering any source change.

messages.author: Kaisa Puro
messages.text: Connector wasn't fully seated. GNSS is reacquired, but offset hasn't returned to baseline yet.

messages.author: Rami Lehto
messages.text: Reacquisition can take time to converge. Monitor against the site's stability criterion; don't call it recovered just because the source indicator is green.

messages.author: Kaisa Puro
messages.text: Offset is inside the acceptance window now and stable for the required interval. Closing with the maintenance note.

messages.author: Meri Halla
messages.text: I'm at the turnoff for SITE-NT-044. The private road has a locked barrier, so I can't reach the cabinet.

messages.author: Joonas Aho
messages.text: I've seen this access constraint before. Stop at a safe place and use the authorized access contact in the work order. Don't bypass the barrier or enter without permission.

messages.author: Meri Halla
messages.text: Coordinator is arranging access with the site owner; no ETA yet.

messages.author: Joonas Aho
messages.text: Pause the dispatch until access is confirmed. Today's approval may only cover this visit. Keep any shared note to the site constraint and approved process—no keys, codes or private contact details.

messages.author: Meri Halla
messages.text: Access confirmed for this work window. Resuming the visit and leaving the recurring access check in the handover.

messages.author: Pekka Niskanen
messages.text: Impact analysis points to AGG-711, but I noticed the topology snapshot predates last week's port move. Can I use it for today's incident?

messages.author: Saara Kivi
messages.text: Treat it as a time-stamped view, not current truth. Compare live neighbor data with the approved change record, and record which snapshot produced the impact result.

messages.author: Pekka Niskanen
messages.text: Live neighbor is AGG-712; the change record confirms the move. CM still has the old relationship.

messages.author: Saara Kivi
messages.text: Update through the normal CM workflow using the move's effective time. Keep the old relationship with its end time so historical impact results remain explainable.

messages.author: Pekka Niskanen
messages.text: Got it. Report now cites the snapshot time and the confirmed mapping correction.
